topicName: Setting up an Angular Development Environment (Node.js, npm/yarn, Angular CLI)
content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Setting up an Angular Development Environment"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"This tutorial guides you through setting up a complete Angular development environment. We'll cover installing Node.js, npm (or yarn), and the Angular CLI."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Prerequisites"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Before you begin, ensure you have a suitable code editor installed. Visual Studio Code is highly recommended due to its excellent Angular support."},{"order":5,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 1: Install Node.js and npm (or yarn)"},{"order":6,"type":"paragraph","text":"Angular requires Node.js. npm (Node Package Manager) is typically bundled with Node.js. Alternatively, you can use yarn as a package manager."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Download Node.js from the official website: <https://nodejs.org/>. Choose the LTS (Long Term Support) version for stability."},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"Verify the installation by opening your terminal or command prompt and running the following commands:"},{"order":9,"type":"code","text":"node -v\nnpm -v"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"If you prefer yarn, install it globally using npm:"},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"npm install -g yarn"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"Verify yarn installation:"},{"order":13,"type":"code","text":"yarn -v"},{"order":14,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 2: Install the Angular CLI"},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"The Angular CLI (Command Line Interface) is a powerful tool for creating, building, and serving Angular applications. Install it globally using npm or yarn:"},{"order":16,"type":"code","text":"npm install -g @angular/cli"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"Or, using yarn:"},{"order":18,"type":"code","text":"yarn global add @angular/cli"},{"order":19,"type":"paragraph","text":"Verify the Angular CLI installation:"},{"order":20,"type":"code","text":"ng version"},{"order":21,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 3: Create a New Angular Project"},{"order":22,"type":"paragraph","text":"Use the Angular CLI to create a new project. Navigate to the directory where you want to create your project and run:"},{"order":23,"type":"code","text":"ng new my-first-app"},{"order":24,"type":"paragraph","text":"The CLI will prompt you for configuration options, such as adding Angular routing and choosing a stylesheet format (CSS, SCSS, etc.)."},{"order":25,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 4: Run the Application"},{"order":26,"type":"paragraph","text":"Navigate to your project directory:"},{"order":27,"type":"code","text":"cd my-first-app"},{"order":28,"type":"paragraph","text":"Start the development server:"},{"order":29,"type":"code","text":"ng serve"},{"order":30,"type":"paragraph","text":"Open your browser and navigate to <http://localhost:4200/>. You should see your new Angular application running."},{"order":31,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":32,"type":"paragraph","text":"You have successfully set up your Angular development environment! You can now start building amazing applications with Angular."}]
